caption:
The secret police watched his apartment and counted the women going inside. Dozens. Every single day. Duchesses and prostitutes in the same queue.

Grigori Rasputin, a Siberian peasant, taught noblewomen that salvation came through sin — the more you sinned, the holier you got. Some kept his dirty underwear as holy relics.

Then he reached the palace. The heir to Russia was a haemophiliac, and this filthy peasant mystic was the only man who could stop the bleeding. The Tsarina worshipped him.

So they decided to kill him. Poisoned cakes. Poisoned wine. He kept eating. They shot him — he got back up. They shot him again and dumped him in the river.

Except none of that happened. The autopsy found no poison, no water in his lungs, and one shot to the forehead. His killer made it up to sell a book.

caption:
Three things everyone repeats about the history of this device. All three are false.

Cleopatra and the gourd full of bees? No ancient source says it. The story was invented in 1992.

Archaeologists really did rebuild a 29,000-year-old stone object from 14 fragments. Eight inches long. It was also used as a hammer.

And the Victorian doctor everyone credits with curing hysteria? He refused to treat women with it, and said so in writing. That story traces back to a single book published in 1999. In 2018 historians checked every source it cited. Not one of them said it.

Both of the myths you believe were invented in your lifetime.

caption:
Two kings shared a bed in 1187 — and had a monk write it down

Richard the Lionheart and Philip of France ate off the same plate and their beds did not separate them at night. It was not a scandal. It was a press release: we are allies, and nobody is getting stabbed tonight.

A bored engineer drew a chastity belt as a joke — it fooled the world 600 years

Konrad Kyeser was writing a manual of war machines in 1405. Between a catapult and a device for turning invisible, he sketched an iron belt. Historians took it seriously for six centuries.

#shorts #history #historyshorts #ancienthistory #forgottenhistory

A Viking woman was divorced for wearing trousers, so she stabbed him in bed

Iceland, around the year 1000. Aud was married to Thord until Thord wanted Gudrun. So she put the trousers back on, rode to his house, and settled it herself. Icelandic law let her.

#shorts #history #historyshorts #ancienthistory #forgottenhistory

In 1726 a woman convinced the King's surgeon she was giving birth to rabbits

Mary Toft was a poor cloth worker. After a miscarriage she began producing pieces of animal flesh, and the local surgeon delivered them himself. The King sent his own man to investigate.

#shorts #history #historyshorts #ancienthistory #forgottenhistory

The emperor's official historian secretly wrote a book calling him a demon

Procopius was court historian to Justinian. His public books praised the emperor's wars and buildings. In private he was writing the Secret History. It surfaced a thousand years later.

#shorts #history #historyshorts #ancienthistory #forgottenhistory

A surgeon practised on 75 poor men before operating on the King of France

In 1686 Louis XIV had a fistula. Nothing the physicians tried worked. So the surgeon rehearsed the operation on seventy-five men from the poorhouses first. Not all of them survived.

#shorts #history #historyshorts #ancienthistory #forgottenhistory

A medieval bride was told to put leeches inside herself the night before her wedding

The instruction came not from a back-street criminal but from a respected medical textbook — the Trotula, compiled in Salerno in the twelfth century.

#shorts #history #historyshorts #ancienthistory #forgottenhistory

Some historians think medieval women chose the back door over losing their virginity

Under the Church's purity laws a woman's worth was settled before she ever spoke. She could be handed to a stranger for land or money, with no say in it.

#shorts #history #historyshorts #ancienthistory #forgottenhistory

The Empress of Rome 'took 25 men in one night' — the truth is worse

Everyone repeats the sex contest. It is a poem, written decades later by a satirist who hated women. What Messalina actually did was more dangerous than anything in the satire.

#shorts #history #historyshorts #ancienthistory #forgottenhistory

If a Spartan husband couldn't give his wife a child, he brought her a younger man

Xenophon wrote it down without a hint of shame. In Sparta a child belonged to the city long before it belonged to a father. Spartan women trained in the open and owned land in their own names.

#shorts #history #historyshorts #ancienthistory #forgottenhistory

He burned a city to kill his wife — then she opened her robe and he dropped the sword

Menelaus spent ten years telling every man at Troy he would kill Helen himself. The horse put him inside the walls. He took her home to Sparta and put her back on the throne.

#shorts #history #historyshorts #ancienthistory #forgottenhistory

The Odyssey opens with its hero as a woman's captive, weeping on a beach

A goddess kept Odysseus on her island for seven years. Homer says he lay in her bed every night because he was not allowed to say no. It took an order from Zeus before she let him go.

#shorts #history #historyshorts #ancienthistory #forgottenhistory

He was told not to read it aloud. It said the King of England had no virility

At the 1536 trials George Boleyn was handed a written allegation that Anne had said Henry VIII had neither skill nor virility. He read every word of it to the court. He was dead two days later.

#shorts #history #historyshorts #ancienthistory #forgottenhistory

His parents were uncle and niece. He could not chew his own food.

Charles II of Spain came out more inbred than a brother-sister child. Europe waited outside his bedroom for an heir that never came, and priests exorcised him for being bewitched.

#shorts #history #historyshorts #ancienthistory #forgottenhistory

The Etruscans shared their wives at dinner — and the Greeks never got over it

If a wife wanted another man at the table, her husband was expected to pour the wine. Nobody in Etruria knew whose child was whose, and nobody seemed to mind.

#shorts #history #historyshorts #ancienthistory #forgottenhistory

Rome had its own Bonnie Blue two thousand years ago — and she was the Empress

The story everyone repeats about her is a satirist's poem, not history. What actually happened was more dangerous, and it ended with a death sentence.

caption:
Russian noblewomen queued outside Rasputin's flat - and their husbands sent them

Every morning a queue formed outside 64 Gorokhovaya Street. Not for the reason the rumours say. They came for favours: promotions, postings, sons pulled out of the war. Rasputin had the Empress's ear, and everyone in Petersburg knew it.

He had earned it doing the one thing Europe's best doctors could not - stopping the heir's bleeding. Alexei was a haemophiliac. Nobody has ever fully explained what Rasputin did at that bedside.

His enemies printed cartoons of him with the Empress in his lap. The story travelled faster than the truth ever could, and it helped bring down a dynasty.

He had a wife back in Siberia. Asked about the other women, she said: he has enough for all.
